chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, all together from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. They said: We asked him about a man who struck another man with a staff and did not desist from him until he died. Is he to be handed over to the guardian of the slain so that he may kill him? He said:
"Yes, and he is not to be left for people to abuse him, but rather the prescribed judgment is to be carried out against him."

key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a staff or stick, indicating the instrument used in the assault
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: struck or beat, referring here to the act of assault
key_terms.وَلِيِّ الْمَقْتُولِ: the guardian or legal heir of the slain person who holds the right in qiṣāṣ
key_terms.يَعْبَثُ بِهِ: to toy with him or abuse him outside proper legal procedure
key_terms.يُجِيزُ عَلَيْهِ: to carry out the due legal judgment against him

ai.seo_question: In a fatal beating case, can the killer be handed over for qiṣāṣ, and may people abuse him before the sentence is carried out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling in a case of fatal assault with a staff, affirming that the killer may be delivered for retaliation. At the same time, it forbids leaving him exposed to uncontrolled abuse, indicating that punishment must proceed through proper legal execution rather than disorderly mistreatment.
